chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both):

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: In what is salvation tomorrow [on the Day of Judgment]? He said: Surely salvation is in not trying to deceive God, lest He deceive you.

For indeed whoever deceives God, He will deceive him and strip faith from him — and he deceives himself, if he but knew. So it was said to him: And how does one deceive God? He said: He does what God has commanded, but intends by it something other than Him.

So fear God and avoid riya' (showing off), for it is shirk (associating partners) with God. Surely the one who shows off will be called by four names on the Day of Resurrection: 'O disbeliever! O transgressor! O treacherous! O loser! Your deeds have fallen void, your reward has been nullified, and there is no share for you today. So seek your reward from the one you were working for.'

key_terms.الرياء: Riya' — showing off or performing worship acts to be seen by others; ostentation
key_terms.النجاة: Al-Naja — salvation; deliverance on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.حبط: Habata — for deeds to fall void, be annulled through corruption of intention
key_terms.خلاق: Khalaq — share, portion, fortune; here meaning no recompense in the Hereafter
key_terms.شرك: Shirk — associating partners with God; here used for the minor/hidden shirk of riya'

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about showing off (riya') in worship?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) warned that performing acts of worship for show (riya') is a form of shirk, as it directs the act toward other than God. This teaching was transmitted through Imam Baqir and Imam Sadiq to later generations. The questioner was told that on the Day of Judgment, the one who performed deeds for show will face four devastating condemnations — disbeliever, transgressor, treacherous, and loser — because their deeds were rendered void by their corrupt intention.
